title: Prefill negotiator and quantization palette: SLO-driven batching defaults and tenant-aware quant profiles
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: Tenant workloads show large variance in the marginal benefit of prefill and aggressive quantization. Default heuristics were conservative which left cost and latency on the table for many production tenants. This PR introduces two cooperating components: (1) a Prefill Negotiator that evaluates request-level SLO constraints, current KV cache hit signals, and a tenant cost budget to decide whether to perform prefill, partial prefill, or prefer streaming without prefill; and (2) a Quantization Palette service that exposes a tenant-aware ranked list of quant profiles (e.g. int8-highfp, int8-fast, int4-safe) plus compatibility metadata so the serving runtime can switch with minimal disruption. Changes are implemented across the serving runtime, control plane, console defaults, and the unit-econ tooling that synthesizes tenant recommendations. Checklist: implement negotiation algorithm and runtime hook, add palette manager and protobufs, persist palette decisions to tenant metadata, add console UI for palette preview and SLO tester, integration tests and canary rollout, add docs and runbook. Rollout plan: staged canary (5% tenant traffic) -> tenant opt-in for 30 days -> auto-apply for low-risk tenants with monitoring guardrails. Related work: builds on ENG-3417 "batching cost probes" and complements recent cache heuristics updates.

tests_summary: Added deterministic unit tests for the negotiator policy and integration tests covering prefill/no-prefill flows, plus compatibility matrix tests exercising quant palette fallbacks. Synthetic workload sim reproduces tenant burstiness and validates amortized cost estimates.
observability_notes: New metrics: prefill_decisions_total{decision=}, prefill_est_cost_delta_histogram, palette_switches_total, palette_fallbacks_total. Added traces in negotiator.evaluate and palette lookup to link decisions with request traces. Dashboards added under Console -> Prefill Insights.
deploy_plan: Canary rollout to routing ring 'theta' (5% live tenants) for 72 hours with alert if prefill_errors>1% or avg latency increase > 15ms for SLO-labeled routes. Step two: opt-in console action for tenants to preview palette and run SLO tester; step three: auto-apply to tenants with low risk after 30-day observation window. Fallback: control-plane lightbox to revert palette per-tenant and global kill-switch via feature flag 'prefill.negotiator.enabled'.
monitoring_and_slo_checks: Monitors created: PrefillDecisionErrorRate > 0.5% alerts to oncall, PaletteFallbackRate > 1% pages to SRE, Unit-Econ drift alert if estimated_cost_delta deviates >20% from observed over 24h. Integration with existing cost telemetry ensures suggested palettes are reconciled with billing data nightly.
release_notes: Introduce tenant-aware prefill negotiator and quantization palette manager. Adds safer default controls for prefill and automated palette recommendations to reduce unit token cost while protecting SLOs. New metrics and a canary rollout with opt-in preview in Console.
post_merge_actions: Create run to validate cost savings across first 100 canary tenants at +7d and +30d windows. Engage solutions engineering to produce a one-pager for high-usage customers. Schedule a postmortem if any of the main SLO alerts trigger during rollout.
notes_for_backport: No breaking API changes; backport to release/2026-02 only for tenants using legacy prefill flags. Apply backport to patch release with tests updating config map schema.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: optimistic prefill decisions could increase tail latency on cold KV stores. Mitigation: negotiator includes a conservative cold-start multiplier, and the canary includes synthetic cold-warm tests. Risk: quant switches may introduce subtle accuracy regressions. Mitigation: palette contains a 'loss_estimate' tag and runtime refuses switch if loss_estimate > tenant threshold.
communication_plan: Announce in #platform and send digest to customers in the next weekly release notes. Add a note in Console changelog with how to preview palettes and opt-in. Coordinate with Sales for any high-usage tenant outreach.
